search_log: Searched "Hell's Corner David Baldacci excerpt first chapter", "point of view third person narrator", Google Books, and the author's site.
Opened the Penguin publisher fragment, which provided an authorized translated opening in sustained third person.
Opened the Google Books record; its accessible page contained metadata, synopsis, and common terms but no sustained prose preview.
Searched exact opening and quote text, including "Oliver Stone was counting the seconds", "There was a time when Stone would have rated", and the sampled first-person lines.
Inspected extended English text at the opening and final page to test for a frame, epistolary structure, or sustained change of person; both remained third person.
Searched "Hell's Corner" with "third person", "point of view", and "narrator"; reviews and catalog pages did not explicitly describe POV, and no credible source indicated alternating narration.
person_note: The controlling narrator presents Oliver Stone and other characters externally in third person. The diagnostic Goodreads passage matches that structure, while the sampled first-person material consists of dialogue, aphorism, or direct character thought. The publisher-hosted Spanish opening independently supports third person, and targeted research found no credible indication of a sustained first-person section, frame, diary, or alternating-person structure. Confidence is med because the authorized evidence is opening-only and translated; the English opening and closing pages come from an unverified text host and are Tier D continuity checks rather than independent corroboration. Audit: independent review retained THIRD but downgraded high to med and corrected both unverified-host entries from Tier C support to Tier D/none.
